_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::fluid_turbulence#0. The physics (DNS needs Kolmogorov-scale resolution, DOFs ~ Re^(9/4)) is not a 4C behaviour and is left alone; what this fixture pins is what 4C actually offers. TURBULENCE_APPROACH has exactly two values, CLASSICAL_LES and DNS_OR_RESVMM_LES, and the default lumps DNS together with residual-VMM LES -- writing 'DNS' is rejected with 'possible values: CLASSICAL_LES|DNS_OR_RESVMM_LES'. 4C never checks resolution and never says 'under-resolved'. The entry's advice to check y+ at the first cell IS actionable, but only through the <output>.flow_statistics file, whose y+ column and '(u_tau)^2 = tau_W/rho' line appear only when DUMPING_PERIOD > 0; the upstream channel deck f3_cha_8x8x8_recongradl2 ships DUMPING_PERIOD: 0 and writes a statistics file with zero data rows. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf).

_mutation.note: remove the pathology from the enum arm: write a value that exists. The rejection and the possible-values line vanish, so the fixture must go red.
_mutation.from: sed 's|^FLUID DYNAMIC/TURBULENCE MODEL:|FLUID DYNAMIC/TURBULENCE MODEL:\n  TURBULENCE_APPROACH: "DNS"|' "$BASE" > "$TMP/dns.yaml"

_mutation.note: remove the pathology from the diagnostics arm: leave DUMPING_PERIOD at the upstream 0, so no y+ rows are ever written. DUMP_STATS_ROWS drops to 0, so the fixture must go red.
